AJ Bell's Nov 3 row is wrong; the event is inside the window (2026-11-02 close to 2026-11-03 close).
conviction_note: Event confirmed as Nov 2 amc. The evidence leans mildly positive (the company has beaten the top of its own revenue guide by 6-9% in recent quarters, consensus sits only 0.8% above the guide top, there are record Q2 US commercial bookings, and the stock de-risked 12% off its record into the print), but almost all of it is public and wire-carried. Puts are at the 97th percentile of their one-year range, and this name has sold off on beats twice in the last four prints (Nov 2025 -7.94%, May 2026 after a $10m US commercial miss). So p_up sits only slightly above 50 (53) on a 12.5% absolute move. The resulting +0.75 is well below the +2.0 findings sum, because the sum counts several small same-direction public items that the reaction function has repeatedly overridden.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: company guide $2.160-2.164bn and adj. op income $1.292-1.296bn (Q2 2026 8-K ex99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321655/000132165526000039/a2026q2ex991pressrelease.htm). Sell-side consensus ~$2.18bn revenue and EPS $0.41 (TipRanks 2026-10-28 https://www.tipranks.com/news/palantir-stock-could-swing-11-65-after-q3-earnings-on-november-2; TradingKey 2026-11-02 https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262263794-palantir-shares-plunge-over-6-ahead-earnings-pltr-tradingkey; CoinCentral 2026-11-01 $2.17-2.18bn, government $1.04bn, 'commercial' $892.1m, https://coincentral.com/palantir-pltr-stock-what-wall-street-expects-from-earnings-monday/). The buy-side bar is probably well above $2.18bn given the beat history, but that is unsourced. The line the stock trades on is US commercial revenue and the FY/Q4 guide (FY2026 currently $8.150-8.158bn revenue, US commercial > $3.424bn).

findings.finding: Palantir has beaten the top of its own revenue guide by wide margins in recent quarters: Q2 2026 revenue was $1.935bn against a $1.797-1.801bn guide (+7.4% over the top) and against the ~$1.80bn consensus. Q1 2026 was $1.633bn against a ~$1.54bn Street estimate (+6%). Q3 2026 consensus of ~$2.18bn sits only ~0.8% above the $2.164bn guide top, so a repeat of the recent beat size (+6-9% over the guide top) implies ~$2.29-2.36bn, or +5-8% against consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a 7.4% beat over the guide top plus a FY raise drove +29.45% close-to-close (optionslam: $125.65 to $162.66). Nov 2025 report: -7.94% despite a beat (TipRanks). May 2026: the stock fell after a 6% revenue beat because US commercial missed StreetAccount's $605m by $10m (Nasdaq/Zacks). So a headline beat by itself has not paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Nine straight beats are widely written about (247wallst 2026-10-14), and the buy-side surely expects a beat over $2.18bn. What would be unpriced is a beat beyond the recent 6-9% range. If the market expected nothing, consensus would sit at the guide and implied vol would be low; instead it is 11.5-13%.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 actuals from a separate document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321655/000132165526000026/a2026q1ex991pressrelease.htm) and the Q2 consensus ($1.80bn) from https://www.itiger.com/news/1123865893. Shares the Q2 8-K with the guidance finding below.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 US commercial bookings were at a record and support Q3 and Q4 US commercial and a further FY raise. US commercial TCV was $2.132bn (+153% Y/Y), and US commercial remaining deal value was $6.238bn (+124% Y/Y, +27% Q/Q). The FY2026 guide was raised from $7.650-7.662bn to $8.150-8.158bn (+~$500m) and US commercial from >$3.224bn to >$3.424bn. The current FY guide implies Q4 revenue of ~$2.42bn (+12% Q/Q over the Q3 guide midpoint), and H2 US commercial of at least $2.065bn against H1's $1.359bn. A third consecutive ~$500m FY raise is the line that bought +29% in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2026 FY raise (+$500m revenue, US commercial guide +$200m) drove +29.45%. May 2026 FY raise (to $7.65bn) was overshadowed by a $10m US commercial miss and the stock fell. The guide and US commercial are the lines this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: The bookings numbers are public since August. What is not knowable is whether management raises by a magnitude that clears a buy-side bar already lifted by the 56% post-August rally. If a big raise were fully priced, the stock would not have fallen 12% off its record into the print with puts at the 97th percentile.
findings.independence: Same document as the beat-pattern finding (Q2 8-K), but a different line (guide and bookings versus reported quarter). Prior guide from the Q1 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321655/000132165526000026/a2026q1ex991pressrelease.htm). The Q2 10-Q shows RPO $4.9bn (43% within 12 months), contract liabilities up from $0.8bn to $1.1bn in H1, and customers 1,049 vs 849 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321655/000132165526000041/pltr-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: The sell-side bar has drifted down at the margin. Zacks reports two analysts cut estimates in the past 30 days, a negative Earnings ESP of -2.44% (its most-accurate estimate sits below consensus), and Rank #3, against the company's record of beating its guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of Zacks ESP predicting PLTR reactions was found. The May 2026 selloff came on a narrow segment miss against StreetAccount, not on headline EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and minor. Its weight is that the most recent revisions are downward, which is not the pattern into a print the market expects to blow out.

findings.finding: Sell-side channel checks into the print are positive. Rosenblatt (McPeake) says its 'checks and proprietary analysis of their customer base point to another beat and raise in 3Q' and raised its target to $260. Morgan Stanley (Equal Weight, $205) says checks point to a potential Q3 revenue beat with limited signs of intensifying competition. Baird expects a 13th consecutive quarter of growth acceleration. JPMorgan initiated at Overweight $262 and put PLTR on positive catalyst watch for the print (all late October 2026).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bullish previews preceded both the +29% (Aug 2026) and the selloffs (Nov 2025, May 2026), so preview tone has not discriminated on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Wire-carried, so mostly priced. The stock fell 5% in the two sessions after these notes (to $184.11), which is what it looks like when holders discount the checks rather than chase them.
findings.independence: TipRanks 2026-10-28 carries the Rosenblatt checks quote independently (https://www.tipranks.com/news/palantir-stock-could-swing-11-65-after-q3-earnings-on-november-2).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is de-risked. The stock closed $184.11 on Oct 30 (-6.27%, fourth straight decline, -7.4% on the week), ~12% below the Oct 9 record close of $209.05, with no company-specific cause reported (TradingKey: 'reducing risk exposure to high-valuation AI stocks'). Puts are at the 97th percentile of the past year and calls at the 76th. Short interest is low (~2.8% of float, 2.3 days in August), so there is no squeeze fuel, but the long base has trimmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Into Aug 2026 the stock was ~40% off its high (TradingKey preview) and rose 29%. Into Nov 2025 it ran near records and fell 7.94%. A pre-print drawdown has preceded the better reaction once in this short record.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself. The case for it is that elevated put demand after a 56% post-August run reads as hedging of gains rather than a fundamental view, so a decent print can unwind the hedges. It is sized small because the options market says the opposite.
findings.independence: CNBC 2026-11-02 on put percentiles (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/02/options-traders-are-getting-anxious-on-palantir-and-apple-ahead-of-earnings.html); price levels in Invezz 2026-10-29.

findings.finding: Independent AI-demand series: Microsoft (reported Oct 28, 2026, quarter to Sep 30) grew Azure 48%, above the 44-45% it guided in July, and commercial RPO grew 73%. It guided Azure to 49-50%. Enterprise AI demand through the September quarter accelerated rather than paused.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of PLTR reacting to hyperscaler prints. PLTR fell 1.6% and 6.3% in the two sessions after MSFT reported.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy: infra consumption is not Palantir's software revenue, and the market saw it and still sold PLTR. Filed small as a macro-to-company transmission that no direct counterparty has confirmed.
findings.independence: Proxy, not this company. A second secondary source has the same numbers (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-microsoft-sees-azure-growing-up-to-50-as-revenue-nears-97b/).

findings.finding: US government demand signals during the quarter: Deputy Defense Secretary Feinberg's Aug 4, 2026 memo (public Aug 11) directs up to ~$243.9m of no-bid Pentagon spending on Palantir services through Mar 31, 2027. Q3 includes the federal fiscal year-end (September). Consensus government revenue of $1.04bn is only +5% Q/Q against Q2's $990m total government revenue, while Q2 US government grew +18% Q/Q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The government line has rarely driven the reaction. US commercial and the guide have (May 2026 fell on US commercial despite 'government strength', per Nasdaq/Zacks).
findings.why_not_priced: The memo is public. The small edge is that a +5% Q/Q government consensus looks low against +18% Q/Q in Q2 and fiscal-year-end seasonality. It is sized small because government revenue is ~half the company and is not the line the stock trades on.
findings.independence: Government consensus from CoinCentral (https://coincentral.com/palantir-pltr-stock-what-wall-street-expects-from-earnings-monday/). The source is an AI-assisted summary of The Register / Federal News Network reporting.

findings.finding: Insider filings into the print: Form 144s were filed Oct 8 (two), Oct 9 and Oct 15, and Form 4s on Oct 13-14, Oct 19 and Oct 30 (three, for Oct 28 transactions), per EDGAR submissions. These look like routine scheduled executive sales; no buys were seen.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Routine Palantir executive selling has not been associated with print reactions in anything found.
findings.why_not_priced: Visible on EDGAR. Filed at zero because the individual filers and the plan status were not read.

findings.finding: Q4 pipeline announcements after the quarter closed: Knox federal-cloud partnership (Oct 19, stock +5% that day), Stagwell expanded AI partnership (Oct 22), Customers Bank collaboration (Oct 15), a 'sovereign AI to new wave of customers' release, Fujitsu AIP/Foundry agreement and Nvidia sovereign-AI work (Sep 10), and the settlement of the London Met Police contract lawsuit (Oct 14). These support a confident Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Partnership headlines move PLTR intraday (Knox +5%) but have not been shown to move the print reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Public. It is worth something only to the extent that management quantifies Q4 TCV from these, which the call may do.

baseline_tension: There is no sealed baseline (bars_failed). Against the externally sourced one, the findings lean mildly positive while the option market is hedged to the downside (puts at the 97th percentile) and the stock fell 12% off its record into the print. The evidence cuts against the skew, which is why p_up is held at 53 rather than the high 50s.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-pattern finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6, because the name sold beats in Nov 2025 and May 2026.
Lesson 7 (positioning is the thing to beat): the de-risked-positioning finding cut from +0.5 to +0.2 because it argues against a 97th-percentile put bid; p_up moved from 54 to 53.
Lesson 1/3 (wire-carried checks): the sell-side checks finding cut from +0.4 to +0.3.
Lesson 5 (narrow proxy): the Microsoft Azure proxy cut from +0.3 to +0.2.

Lesson 2/6: lands_on and the bar checked. The guidance finding stands at +0.5 because the guide is the line that paid (+29% in Aug). The bar is sourced to the company guide plus agreeing consensus, so no cap was applied.
Lesson 9: the government finding is held small because it is ~half the company and not the trading line. The insider and partnership findings are unchanged.
